# Sāriputta Sutta (Snp 4.16 (PTS Snp 185))

**ID:** Snp 4.16 (PTS Snp 185)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sāriputta Sutta* (Snp 4.16, verses 955–975), also titled *Therapañha Sutta* ("The Elder's Questions"), is the sixteenth and concluding discourse of the *Aṭṭhakavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* [Fronsdal 2016; Norman 1997-2001; Nyanaponika, Hecker, Bodhi 2003]. The text consists of an opening set of verses praising the Buddha followed by a series of questions posed by the venerable Sāriputta regarding the fears, hazards, and monastic training of a monk living in seclusion to eliminate mental defilements, together with the Buddha's corresponding replies [Fronsdal 2016; Nyanaponika, Hecker, Bodhi 2003].

The discourse is of notable historical and epigraphical interest, as it is widely identified with the *Upatisa-pasina* ("Upatissa's Question") recommended to monastics and laity by Emperor Aśoka in his third-century BCE Bhabru (Calcutta-Bairat) rock edict, Upatissa being Sāriputta's personal name [Bhattacharya 1948; Fronsdal 2016; Norman 1997-2001; Thomas 1933]. If this identification is accepted, it establishes that the sutta existed and was recognized as authoritative prior to 232 BCE [Fronsdal 2016].

Curated parallels include a passage-level Chinese parallel preserved in the *Arthapada Sūtra* (T 198) and a resembling passage in the Jain work *Isibhāsiyāiṁ* 38.6. The sutta is commented upon line-by-line in the canonical *Mahāniddesa* under the title *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16), which interprets the opening verse as referring to the Buddha's descent from the Tāvatimsa heaven after preaching the Abhidhamma [Nyanaponika, Hecker, Bodhi 2003]. DharmaNexus registers 103 Pali text-reuse matches, most extensively with Mnd 16 (90 matches, including §9.1–11.1), as well as recurrent matches with the *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* and *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records machine-generated cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Ārya-bodhisattvapiṭaka-nāma-mahāyānasūtra* (D0056) [DharmaNexus].
